$description: Behavioural conformance for the auri insight catalog. A contract says which props exist; these cases say what a renderer must DO with them. Any renderer claiming this catalog id must pass every case. Elements are addressed by role and accessible name, so a case is only executable if the rendered result is accessible.

cases.why: drillAction is registered `raw` precisely so the component can merge subjectKind and subjectId into the context before dispatch — the agent is told never to duplicate them itself. A port that dispatches the bare wire action sends an event naming no subject, so the agent cannot tell WHICH finding was opened. It fails silently: an action still fires, it just means nothing.

Two obligations at once. The verdict is merged like the subject, and the card must VISIBLY change — DESIGN.md section 8, contributed by the first consumer: feedback that changes nothing on screen teaches users their input is decorative, and they stop giving it. A port may restyle the acknowledgement but may not omit it.

A model emitting 0.8 is claiming precision it does not have. The contract carries the raw number so the renderer can decide, and the renderer must show a qualitative band. A port that prints the number — or a percentage — turns a hedge into a false measurement.

subjectKind and signalType are free strings (contract principle 9): what a finding is about is the consumer's vocabulary, not ours. This catalog previously formatted signalType through a fixed label table and rendered NOTHING for an unlisted value — a valid emission silently lost on the way to the screen. Any value must survive to the UI, humanized but never dropped.

Raw values on the wire: the agent sends 1200000 and the ISO 4217 code, never a pre-formatted string it guessed a locale for. `unit` follows the same convention as ops Stat so one figure reads identically across catalogs. A port that concatenates the code onto the number produces 'USD 1200000' and loses both grouping and placement.

The focus contract. Levels are kept MOUNTED-BUT-HIDDEN rather than destroyed, so the element a user drilled from still exists to return to; a port that keys the levels and remounts them destroys that target and strands keyboard and screen-reader users at the top of the document. Drill in, come back, and focus must be exactly where it was. This was found by a browser test on its first run, not by review.
